definition: A software-defined computer with its own virtual CPU, RAM, disk, and network card that runs a full guest operating system on a physical host.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 21: Virtualization Concepts

definition: An isolated, often temporary environment where untrusted programs or new code run without touching the host system; it is discarded and starts clean each time.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 21: Virtualization Concepts

definition: Using virtual machines to try work-in-progress applications on the same or a different operating system without risking a production computer.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 11: Virtualization and Cloud Computing

definition: Running one program in a virtual environment instead of installing it on the local operating system, for example to keep an old or foreign-platform app working.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 11: Virtualization and Cloud Computing

definition: Old, outdated programs that often run only on an older operating system, so a business keeps them working inside a virtual machine of that older system.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 11: Virtualization and Cloud Computing

definition: Letting a program built for one operating system or hardware platform run on a different one, such as a macOS app inside a virtual machine on a Windows server.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 11: Virtualization and Cloud Computing

definition: Separating a user's desktop environment from the physical computer so the desktop, its OS, and its apps run virtually and can be reached from another device.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 21: Virtualization Concepts

definition: Server-based system, on-premises or in the cloud, that hosts many users' virtual desktops, builds the desktop images, and gives clients network access to them.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 21: Virtualization Concepts

definition: Software that imitates specific hardware or firmware, even a different processor, without a hypervisor or the CPU's own virtualization features.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 21: Virtualization Concepts

definition: Software, also called a virtual machine manager, that lets several guest operating systems share one physical computer and allocates its CPU, memory, and storage to them.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 11: Virtualization and Cloud Computing

definition: Bare-metal virtualization layer installed straight on the server hardware with no host OS, such as VMware ESXi; it is faster but needs a proper server.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 21: Virtualization Concepts

definition: Hosted virtualization software that runs on top of an existing operating system, such as VirtualBox or VMware Workstation, so guests are one layer further from the hardware.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 21: Virtualization Concepts

definition: The operating system installed on the physical computer under a hosted hypervisor; if it fails, every virtual machine running on it fails too.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 11: Virtualization and Cloud Computing

definition: An operating system installed inside a virtual machine, running on virtual hardware that a hypervisor provides.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 21: Virtualization Concepts

definition: A lightweight package of one application and its runtime dependencies that shares the host's OS kernel instead of running a full OS, as with Docker or Podman.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 21: Virtualization Concepts

definition: The file a developer builds that holds an app plus all the libraries and settings it needs, which a container engine such as Docker then runs.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 11: Virtualization and Cloud Computing

definition: A software network adapter that a hypervisor gives each virtual machine, which can link to other guests or, through a virtual switch, to the physical adapter.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 11: Virtualization and Cloud Computing

definition: A software device inside the hypervisor that forwards traffic between virtual machines' adapters and can attach them to the host's physical network card.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 11: Virtualization and Cloud Computing

definition: VM network mode that connects the guest straight to the host's physical network, so the guest needs its own IP address on that external network.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 21: Virtualization Concepts

definition: Common default VM network mode in which guests get addresses on a separate private network but still reach the external network and Internet through the host.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 21: Virtualization Concepts

definition: VM network mode that creates a private virtual network where guests can talk to each other and the host but not to the external network.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 21: Virtualization Concepts

definition: CPU feature, Intel VT-x or AMD-V, that must be supported and enabled in BIOS/UEFI before a hypervisor such as Hyper-V will install or start guests.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 11: Virtualization and Cloud Computing

definition: Virtual drive that starts small and grows only as the guest writes data, up to the maximum size chosen, which saves space on the host drive.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 21: Virtualization Concepts

definition: Virtual drive that takes all of its chosen capacity, for example 60 GB, on the host drive as soon as it is created.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 21: Virtualization Concepts

definition: Problem where the number of VMs grows beyond what administrators can control, so they slip out of change and life cycle management.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 21: Virtualization Concepts

definition: Attack in which code inside a guest breaks out of its isolation and interacts with the host or hypervisor; patching the virtualization software prevents it.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 21: Virtualization Concepts

definition: A saved copy of a virtual machine's exact state at one moment, so the guest can be rolled back to that point after a failed test or change.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Glossary; checked against CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 21: Virtualization Concepts

definition: Using on-demand services, such as storage, applications, or servers, that a provider runs on remote, virtualized hardware and delivers over a network connection.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 22: Cloud Computing Concepts

definition: Cloud deployment that a provider such as Amazon or Microsoft offers to anyone over the Internet, giving low cost and high scalability but less control.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 22: Cloud Computing Concepts

definition: Cloud deployment built for one organization, often in its own data center, giving it the most control over security and data but the highest cost.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 22: Cloud Computing Concepts

definition: Cloud deployment that combines an organization's own private servers with a third party's public services, usually keeping confidential data in-house.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 22: Cloud Computing Concepts

definition: Cloud deployment shared by several organizations with common interests or requirements, such as hospitals, which know and trust the other members.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 22: Cloud Computing Concepts

definition: Cloud service model that rents servers, storage, networking, and VM hosting; the client installs and manages the operating systems and software, which takes the most expertise.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 22: Cloud Computing Concepts

definition: Cloud service model that adds operating systems and development tools on top of rented hardware so programmers can build, test, and deploy their own apps.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 22: Cloud Computing Concepts

definition: Cloud service model where users run finished applications, such as webmail or Microsoft 365, over the Internet without installing or maintaining them locally.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 22: Cloud Computing Concepts

definition: Billing in which the customer can draw on nearly unlimited cloud resources but pays only for the amount actually used, such as storage, bandwidth, or CPU time.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 22: Cloud Computing Concepts

definition: Data moving into the cloud from outside, such as uploads or syncing on-premises systems; most providers do not charge for it.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 22: Cloud Computing Concepts

definition: Data leaving the cloud for outside destinations, such as downloads or streaming to users; providers often charge for it.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 22: Cloud Computing Concepts

definition: The ability to scale cloud resources up quickly when demand grows and back down when it falls, without buying or selling hardware.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 11: Virtualization and Cloud Computing

definition: Cloud characteristic that lets a customer add storage or processing automatically, without waiting for anyone at the provider to act.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 11: Virtualization and Cloud Computing

definition: Cloud setup in which many customers draw from one pool of the provider's servers, storage, and bandwidth and each pays for the share it uses.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 11: Virtualization and Cloud Computing

definition: Cloud setup in which a single customer has exclusive use of a server's or infrastructure's whole capacity, as in a private cloud.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 22: Cloud Computing Concepts

definition: Cloud characteristic in which many customers run on the same physical hardware, storage, and network while each one's data and operations stay isolated.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 22: Cloud Computing Concepts

definition: The uptime a cloud provider guarantees in its service level agreement, often stated in nines, such as 99.99 percent.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 11: Virtualization and Cloud Computing

definition: Cloud characteristic that keeps the newest copy of each file both in cloud storage and on local devices, updating one copy whenever the other changes.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 11: Virtualization and Cloud Computing
